ED Security Panic At Manicaland State University
29 September 2026
Share
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:28
Instaread

By A Correspondent | Manicaland State University of Applied Sciences has issued an unusually stringent security warning ahead of Friday’s graduation ceremony, which will be presided over by President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

TourColleges

In a notice circulated on its social media platforms, the university listed a wide range of items that will be prohibited at the graduation venue, warning that anyone who compromises security will face the consequences.

Discover more

Access Services

Among the banned items are pens, pins, razor blades, firearms, matches, placards, markers, power banks, notebooks, umbrellas, explosives, knives, lipstick, face-makeup kits, chemicals and cigarette lighters.

The university said any prohibited items discovered at the entrance would be confiscated and kept at the security desk until the owners leave the venue.

TourColleges

“Any prohibited item found will be held at the security desk until you leave. Items left at the security desk are at the owner’s risk, and MSUAS accepts no responsibility for loss or damage,” the university said.

The unusually extensive list has raised eyebrows, particularly the inclusion of ordinary items such as pens, notebooks, power banks, lipstick and makeup kits alongside weapons, explosives and other potentially dangerous materials.

The heightened security comes against the backdrop of years of heightened concern around the security of President Mnangagwa at major public gatherings.

CompareSecurity

Mnangagwa came to power in November 2017 following a military coup that ended Robert Mugabe’s presidency. The military at the time said it was targeting individuals around Mugabe and insisted that the president and his family were safe.

Within months of Mnangagwa taking office, security concerns became more pronounced.

On June 23, 2018, a grenade exploded at White City Stadium in Bulawayo shortly after Mnangagwa had addressed a ZANU-PF campaign rally. The president escaped unharmed, but the blast injured dozens of people, including senior government officials. Reuters reported at the time that Mnangagwa said a grenade had been thrown at him, while investigations involving the police, army and intelligence services were launched.

The attack prompted a tightening of security around the President at public gatherings. Contemporary reports documented body searches, sniffer dogs, scanners and restricted access at subsequent events.

There have also been other reported security breaches around presidential events. In August 2018, for example, a serving soldier was reportedly arrested after attempting to enter Heroes Acre with a loaded handgun shortly before Mnangagwa arrived for Heroes Day commemorations.

CompareSecurity

The security concerns have continued to shape the organisation of major events involving the President, with extensive police, military and intelligence deployments reported at some public gatherings.

Mnangagwa, who is Chancellor of Zimbabwe’s state universities, has regularly presided over graduation ceremonies at public universities. In recent years, he has attended graduation ceremonies at institutions including the University of Zimbabwe, Midlands State University, the National University of Science and Technology and Manicaland State University of Applied Sciences.

MSUAS itself held its third graduation ceremony in December 2024, with Mnangagwa attending as Chancellor and capping 153 graduates.

The university has urged all stakeholders attending Friday’s ceremony to familiarise themselves with the prohibited-items list before arriving at the venue.

The restrictions are expected to result in additional security checks at entry points as authorities seek to prevent prohibited items from reaching the graduation venue.

CompareSecurity

For students and their families, however, the extensive list means that ordinary personal belongings that would normally be carried into a graduation ceremony will have to be left behind.

The university has urged attendees to comply with the measures to ensure a safe and orderly ceremony.
